en: Sutta Nipāta 4.7 Tissametteyyasutta “For one who is devoted to sexual intercourse, [there is no escape from suffering].”
"Thus spoke the venerable Tissa Metteyya:
'Speak of affliction, dear sir;
having heard your instruction,' "
“We shall train in seclusion.
“For one devoted to sexual intercourse,” said the Blessed One, “Metteyya, [there is no training in seclusion].”
Or even if you must uphold the teaching,
yet you practice wrongly—
this is what makes one ignoble in that regard.
He who, having previously practiced alone,
now indulges in sexual intercourse,
is like a wandering carriage in this world.
They call the worldling base;
whatever fame and renown he previously had,
that too diminishes for him.
Having seen this as well,
one should train to abandon sexual intercourse;
for he is beset by his own thoughts.
He broods like one who is wretched;
having heard the reproach of others,
such a person becomes dejected.
If, being challenged by the doctrines of others,
one then engages in disputes,
this indeed is his great snare.
He plunges into what is censured by the wise;
though designated as "wise," he is intent upon a solitary life.
Yet even one engaged in sexual intercourse wallows like a fool;
having understood this danger, [one should abandon it].
A sage here, regarding what precedes and what follows,
should make a firm resolve for solitary practice and should not indulge in sexual intercourse.
One should train in discernment alone;
this is the supreme quality of the noble ones.
One should not, on account of that, consider oneself superior.
He is indeed close to Nibbāna—
when the sage lives empty-minded,
having no longing for sensual pleasures.
"People who are obsessed with sensual pleasures long for one who has crossed over the flood.
Thus ends the seventh discourse, the Tissa Metteyya Sutta.
